lines.text: Which one is the patient?
Both. Wonderful. Aigoo. (Oh dear.)
You: bed. You: chair. No, the CHAIR.
The bed is for sick people. You are only foolish.
Pen torch. My top pocket. Hold it HERE.
Shake, and I stitch your sleeve to his face.
Two tablets after food. Not 'vibes'.
And drink water. Both of you. Did I stutter?
My number. Do NOT call for nonsense.
Caller. Energy drink is not breakfast.
Caller. CALLER. I can hear you opening one.
Excuse me. Is that my PATIENT reading the news?
THE HOSPITAL LINE DROPS EVERY NIGHT. 01:17.
I HAVE BABIES ON MACHINES. THIS IS NOT NONSENSE.
…sorry. I know you have exams. Who else do I ask?
Your helmet is on backwards.
This explains a great deal about you.
…Thank you. I mean it.
That old man is in the garden again.
No. I will not tell you which ward.
Confidentiality is not a suggestion.
He comes. He sits. He never comes in.
Forty minutes of diesel. The tanker comes at five.
How many forty minutes between now and five?
Good. So we make diesel appear. You carry.
I asked you for one thing. One.
I did not ask you to think at me.
Six children. I know to the watt what each one needs.
And you are standing in my ward with a plan.
Listen with your ears. Not your mouth. Carry.
And another thing. When I say carry, the correct—
That is what your NEPA jokes cost.
Whatever you people do at night, with your torches.
I don't want to know. Fix it.
I'm not crying. It's the ramyeon. It's spicy.
Read it. I can't. I've asked for the coast.
Of all the places in Nigeria. I can see the ROOF.
Aigoo.
Fine. Somebody must keep you people alive. Drink water.
It's not laziness. Don't say 'cheer up'.
Sit with them. Then outside. Small, small.
Just sit. It's harder than it sounds. Did I stutter?
Eighty-two. And one goat, who is not a patient. Yet.
You. Cards. Red now, yellow soon, green waits.
Listen with your ears, not your mouth. No.
Why is that tap dripping? Who allowed that tap?
You did well. Both of you. Drink water.
Before my time. Some visitors never sign. Close it.
Six months. If he listens.
Does he listen?
Hauwa needs hands. Don't argue with her. I don't.
I have an offer. A fellowship. Paediatrics. In Seoul.
I haven't decided. Don't decide for me.
Drink water. You've been digging. Did I stutter?
Good. Now burn the socks. Doctor's orders.
I was told there would be no patients.
You look pale. Sit. No. I'm off. …Drink water.
Kimchi does that at the hospital too.
At the garden bench. …What is she looking at?
Do NOT jump on him! The knee! Aigoo!
Sit. The chair. You know the rule about the bed.
I answer Seoul by six. You are here as company.
Company. Not counsel. Did I stutter?
Aigoo. [Oh dear.] Come. Listen with your ears.
Who is your friend?
Have we met? You look like someone I see here.
Which patient's… No. Confidentiality.
I'll tell you after your exams.
You listened. All night. I noticed.
Go and sleep. Doctor's orders.
Don't draw it. Loosen the bolt. Listen with your ears.
They can wait a day. These ones can't.
One: thirty minutes of diesel. Two: children upstairs.
Three: bring me light. And people. Did I stutter?
Hwaiting. [You can do it.] Drink water. Go.
One hour. Then I am back on my ward. Move.
Medicine. For whoever keeps the lights on. Drink water.
Aigoo. [Oh dear.] Look at you in a gown. Stand straight.
I came from the airport. Did you drink water?
Annyeong. [Hi.] Did you drink water?
You again. What did you do?
Hello. Sit. No, the chair.
Bap meogeosseo? [Have you eaten?] Don't lie to me.
My favourite repeat customer. Second favourite. Jega's first.
Jalja. [Sleep well.] Real sleep. Not phone sleep.
Go. Drink water on the way.
Bye. Don't come back injured.
Hwaiting! [You can do it!] Now go.
Gomawo. [Thanks.] You were useful today. Rare.
Thank you. I mean it. Don't make a face.
Mianhae. [Sorry.] I snapped. Night shift does that.
Sorry. I was sharp. I'm tired, not angry.
Good. You listened. Look at you, growing.
Nice shirt. Sit up straight in it.
Daebak. [Amazing.] I'm genuinely impressed.
Your socks. Explain your socks.
You walk like someone who skipped breakfast. Did you?
You look like a K-drama second lead. Tired and hopeful.
You called me Snow White? Fine. Then you're Dopey.
Walk faster. Children don't wait for slow people.
Stay close. The TH corridors eat freshers.
Keep up. I've done thirty hours. You've done breakfast.
Ppalli ppalli. [Hurry, hurry.] Did I stutter?
I'm counting. My patients can't wait. Hurry.
Wrong ward. That's Orthopaedics. Turn around.
That's the pharmacy queue. You'll be there till Year 3.
Yes. Doctor's orders.
Ne. [Yes.] Obviously.
Yes. And drink water.
No. Did I stutter?
Absolutely not. Medically, morally, no.
Ani. [No.] Next question.
Maybe. After my shift. Ask me in twelve hours.
Possibly. Bring snacks and I'll think faster.
Jinjja? [Really?] Explain that again. Slowly.
I've seen a lot. I have not seen that.
Correct. Finally, a sensible patient.
Yes. That. Exactly that.
No sick note for 'vibes'.
I don't prescribe for heartbreak. Drink water.
Kimchi bit the curtain. Suya watched. Accomplice.
My K-drama: a doctor sleeps eight hours. Pure fantasy.
When did you last eat? Real food. Garri doesn't count.
Two tablets after food. Which food? Name it.
Gwaenchana? [Are you okay?] Honestly.
Daebak! [Amazing!] Hwaiting worked!
Told you. Drink water, then celebrate.
Aigoo. [Oh dear.] Okay. We go again tomorrow.
Losing is a symptom, not a diagnosis.
Excuse me. I'm holding a syringe.
Careful. I bruise, and I remember.
Don't move. Wiggle your toes. Good. Now get up.
Aigoo. [Oh dear.] Gravity wins again.
Light's gone. Generator in ninety seconds. Count with me.
NEPA. Not now. Never now.
Dark again. Kimchi will think it's bedtime.
Light. Thank God. The monitors are back.
Up NEPA. Now please stay.
Rain. More malaria next week. I'm stocking up.
Rain and ramyeon. The only cure I believe in.
Heat like this, you drink water. Every hour. Every.
Forty degrees. My scrubs have become a sauna.
Instant ramyeon in the call room. Fine dining.
Suya! …The food. Not the cat. Don't tell the cat.
Tteokbokki [spicy rice cakes] would cure everything. Nobody sells it.
House officer salary. Delayed. Like everything else.
Sapa reached the hospital. Even the doctors.
A cat sticker! Kimchi will hate it. I love it.
Snacks. You understand me.
An energy drink? For a doctor? Bold.
Thank you. …I'll give this to Hauwa.
Korean snacks? Where did you— Gomawo! [Thanks!]
A cat toy! Suya says thank you. Kimchi will steal it.
Kimchi, saranghae. [I love you.] Do not touch the curtains.
Thirty-six hours awake. I can hear colours.
Episode eleven. He's about to confess. I'm on call.
Suya, get off the keyboard. That's my handover.
Night shift. Ramyeon, a drama, and nine babies.
Shh. The ward is finally asleep. Breathe quietly.
Fresher! You look healthy. Suspicious.
Oh, the goat-chasing one. Hello.
First-year malaria. A rite of passage. Take your drugs.
You've lost weight. That's not a compliment. Eat.
Exams? You're pale. Drink water. Then read.
House officer. House. Officer. I live here now.
Ward round at six. I woke at five fifty-eight.
Ask Dr. Z? Never heard of her. Drink water.
Hauwa says sit. I sit. Everybody sits for Hauwa.
Kimchi learnt to open the fridge. I'm raising a criminal.
Pen torch, top pocket. Always. Ask Jega why.
That eyebrow healed nicely. My stitching, not his luck.
You held the pen torch steady. Don't let it go to your head.
The bed is for sick people. Still true. Still you.
Energy drink is not breakfast. I'm still saying it.
My PATIENT, reading the news. Aigoo. [Oh dear.]
I shouted about the line. Sorry. Not about the babies.
Jega lost the final and came for paracetamol. Loyal.
01:17. The lights blink. Every night. I hate 01:17.
Night calls. Ramyeon. Sleep is a K-drama myth.
Firdausi asked about medicine. I gave her a warning and a glove.
Jega, head one more goalpost and I'll name a ward after you.
Ah. Alive. Good. Keep it that way.
You hit a pothole on an okada? Nobody is surprised.
A candle date? Bring candles AND a torch.
Second year of shouting at your friends. Same friends.
Housemanship ends soon. I'll miss nothing. Except Hauwa.
The mall has light all night. My ward has forty minutes.
Hauwa ate my ramyeon. I've reported it to nobody.
Helmet backwards. I still laugh about it at night.
Posting letter soon. National service. Please, the coast.
Firdausi shadowed me today. She didn't faint. Hire her.
Suya sat on my stethoscope. He's a doctor now.
Helmet. Front. Facing forward. We practised.
That old man? Patient confidentiality is not a suggestion.
Which ward? I like you. Still no.
Forty minutes of diesel. I count to forty in my sleep.
You carried. All night. I noticed. Don't tell anyone.
Whatever you people do at night: it worked. Don't tell me.
Of all the places in Nigeria. {{TOWN}}. I can see the roof.
I'm not crying. Spicy ramyeon. Still the excuse.
Generator hours. I know them like K-pop lyrics.
Still on campus in the strike? Did you eat today?
Strike diet: garri, garri, regret. I can see it on you.
You've been reading? In a strike? Who are you?
Eighty-two patients. One goat. The goat is not a patient.
Your lecturers strike. Fevers don't.
Red now. Yellow soon. Green waits. Even uncles.
Who allowed that tap? It drips. I hear it in my sleep.
The clinic has one fan. Three blades. Two work.
I check my email. I close my email. I check it.
Mental health is health. Not weakness. Did I stutter?
I'm fine. Doctors are fine. Doctors are always fine.
Sit with them. Just sit. You did. Good.
Firdausi heard a whole heart. I heard her hear it.
Old register, odd signatures. Not my business. Close it.
Six months. If he listens. Is he listening?
Tell Jega: the knee doesn't care about prize money.
You did nights with Hauwa? You're stronger than me.
I said I haven't decided. Stop looking at me like that.
Kimchi sleeps on the letter from Seoul. She has opinions.
The clinic generator has opinions. So do I.
Welcome to Paediatrics. You're the tallest patient here.
IT student? You look like an intern. Tired and lost.
Nusaiba made me sign three petitions before breakfast.
Junior resident, Paediatrics. Small patients. Big opinions.
Children cry, I sing. Badly. In Korean. It works.
Cold ramyeon. Unsent email. Ward round. Normal Tuesday.
Back at the TH. Same corridors. Different me.
Lollipops after injections. Policy. Mine.
Annyeong, little one. [Hi.] Doctor is here. No crying.
Hwaiting! [You can do it!] One more spoon. Good.
I have an email to send. Not today.
Campaign posters on my ward door? Nusaiba. Down. Now.
Burn the socks. I said it. I meant it.
No patients, they said. Touch grass, they said. Sit.
Why do cats stare at empty benches? Don't answer.
Do NOT jump on his knee! …You jumped. Aigoo. [Oh dear.]
Firdausi named an eel after me. I'm choosing to be flattered.
You listened. All night. I noticed.
Which button? After your exams. That was the deal.
Night on the children's ward. Twelve snores. All tiny.
Finalist! Stand straight. You'll have a gown soon.
Your final year. Also an important year for me. Drink water.
Defence nerves? Breathe out longer than in. Doctor's orders.
Kimchi and Suya are learning to share. Slowly. Like you lot.
Somebody has to keep you people alive until convocation.
I keep a list of your injuries. It's long. Lovingly.
Five years ago you chased a goat. Look at you now.
Gwaenchana? [Are you okay?] Finals do that. Eat.
I'm proud of you. I'll say it once. Write it down.
Hauwa says I'm soft now. I've reported her to nobody.
Hwaiting! [You can do it!] Last papers. Then sleep a week.
Your project smoked on the lawn. Symptom: ambition.
Don't draw it. Loosen the bolt. Shamsu hasn't forgiven me.
They could wait a day. The children couldn't.
Daebak. [Amazing.] You brought everybody.
One hour off the ward. For the lights. Worth it.
Alhaji Needle delivered on time. A medical miracle.
Defence done? Pulse check. Fast. Normal. Congratulations.
Last nights before convocation. Sleep. That's an order.
Medicine, graduate entry. Firdausi. I'm not crying. Ramyeon.
Annyeong from Seoul. [Hi from Seoul.] Did you drink water?
Seoul has cat cafés. I've been to nine. For research.
It's cold here. I miss NEPA. …No, I don't.
Snow White in real snow. Yes, I see the joke.
Freshers, the TH is not a hangout. Except the canteen.
Malaria season meets freshers' week. My busiest week.
Panic is real. Breathe with me. In. Out. Again.
No energy drinks. No all-nighters. …Fine. One.
Whatever the results say, eat lunch.
A bad grade is not a diagnosis.
Allowance came? Buy fruit. One fruit. It's a start.
Market day. I'm here for oranges and gossip.
Hajiya Ladi asked for a free consult. She paid in tomatoes.
Strike again? Use it. Sleep. Eat. Read one page.
Cup final. I'm on standby. With ice packs. For Jega.
Do not head it like that. Do NOT. …Aigoo. [Oh dear.]
Vote. Then drink water. Civic duty and hydration.
Nusaiba made me sign three things. One was a pledge.
Convocation. I'll cry. It will be the ramyeon again.
Snow White came to see her favourite people graduate.
Break your fast with water and dates, not five puff-puffs.
Iftar on the ward. Hauwa brought dates. We shared.
Christmas on call. Pastor Sam brought jollof. Bless him.
Valentine's? I'm dating a call rota. It's complicated.
Flowers for a doctor? Cat food for her cats. Smarter.
Harmattan. Lips, lotion, water. In that order.
Dust season. Asthma clinic is full. Don't add yourself.
